messages:
Sara (PM): quick sync — need to prioritise two private-deploy asks from sales: preserve customer egress IPs for long-lived tenants, and a zero-downtime upgrade path for air-gapped installs. what are minimal launch criteria?
Chen (Eng Lead): +1. can we scope M1 (launch) vs M2 (followup)? M1 should guarantee egress IP preservation for the common operator setups. M2 can add live kv-sync for rolling upgrades.
Diego (SRE): preserving egress IPs is mostly about installer + node affinity logic. timeline depends on whether we require external control-plane changes. zero-downtime is harder — KV cache migration across versions is the pain point.
Maya (Field): acme and finco customers flagged both as showstoppers. Acme says they need no-IP-change in cutover window <= 2h. they prefer an installer knob rather than manual netops.
Lucas (Solutions): installer knob = `--preserve-egress` + clear doc. also we should ship a troubleshooting script: `redwoodctl network-check`. customers want preflight that simulates IP handoff.
Chen (Eng Lead): tech notes: to ensure IP preservation across upgrades we need: 1) consistent node labels, 2) deterministic host selection, 3) a graceful drain that keeps service endpoints stable. Could be done without control-plane changes if we extend operator. est: 3 sprint engineering.
Diego (SRE): zero-downtime upgrade options: A) in-place rolling with KV migration (complex), B) dual-read-side-by-side (requires extra resources), C) blue-green with IP handoff (network trickery). For on-prem with strict egress, blue-green + VIP failover is safest.
Maya (Field): customers with strict egress prefer solution C. but many small customers can't afford double capacity. need a fallback: scheduled maintenance with IP-preservation checkpoint.
Sara (PM): proposing launch buckets: M1 (GA): egress-preservation installer + preflight + docs + `--preserve-egress`; M1-limited: scheduled maintenance rollback playbook. M2: blue-green VIP + KV live migration + smaller-memory agent for low-capacity sites. agree?
Chen (Eng Lead): agree on M1 scope. implement operator-side labels + drain hooks. M2 dependent on runtime KV migration infra — needs research spike.
Lucas (Solutions): I'll draft preflight UX text and two sample `redwoodctl` runs for field demos. Also propose a `minimal-agent` packaging variant for low-capacity customers for M2 planning.
Diego (SRE): we also need observability SLAs for upgrade: per-tenant latency/failure checks + rollback thresholds. I'll add an alert playbook.
Maya (Field): will collect 3 anchor customers for beta (Acme, FinCo, EdgeHost). will run acceptance checklist and capture netops runbook feedback.
Sara (PM): launch criteria checklist (proposed):
- installer supports `--preserve-egress` and preserves IP for operator-managed clusters (stringent tests)
- preflight that simulates egress handoff + expected outputs in doc
- rollback playbook validated with 2 pilot customers
- public docs + customer-facing runbook + support triage path
- telemetry: install success/failure + upgrade-rollback events emitted
If all green -> signoff for M1 GA.
Chen (Eng Lead): add unit/integration test targets: simulate edge NAT + affinty scenarios. We should have CI matrix with 3 network topologies.
Diego (SRE): add a canary plan: start with non-critical tenants, metric windows 30m, auto-rollback on error rates > 2x baseline.
Sara (PM): ok owners: Chen -> impl, Diego -> rollout & playbook, Lucas -> preflight UX + scripts, Maya -> customer pilots, Sara -> docs + launch comms. timeline: aim for 3 sprints for M1.
Maya (Field): I'll open pilot requests and schedule cutovers. customers asked for a sample IP-preserve checklist — Lucas pls prioritize.
Lucas (Solutions): on it. I'll post initial scripts in #docs later today.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: private-installer-v0.9.1 -> staging (build 482).
Chen (Eng Lead): small note: if we expose a `--preserve-egress` flag, we must clearly document limitations (HA mode, multi-AZ, operator downtimes). otherwise support load will spike.
Sara (PM): noted — include an explicit "limitations" section in the runbook.
Maya (Field): can we get a short slide for sales to use on the pilot page? 2 bullets: what we guarantee + what we recommend prep-wise.
Sara (PM): Lucas take that as follow-up.
Chen (Eng Lead): final ask — need product approval on M1 resource constraints: we will not guarantee zero-cost for blue-green. M1 promise is IP preservation w/ scheduled window fallback.
Sara (PM): agreed. we'll call out cost/scale tradeoffs in the launch page. thanks all — next sync Thurs 10am to review pilot results and CI pass status.
